answer:
Cylinder volume:
\[
V_c=AH=(50\text{ cm}^2)(40\text{ cm})=2000\text{ cm}^3=2.00\times10^{-3}\text{ m}^3
\]

Cylinder mass:
\[
m_c=\rho_c V_c=(750)(2.00\times10^{-3})=1.50\text{ kg}
\]

With the \(0.300\text{ kg}\) load:
\[
m_{\text{total}}=1.50+0.300=1.80\text{ kg}
\]

For floating, displaced water mass equals total mass, so
\[
V_d=\frac{m_{\text{total}}}{\rho_w}
=\frac{1.80}{1000}=1.80\times10^{-3}\text{ m}^3
=1800\text{ cm}^3
\]

Submerged height:
\[
h_{\text{sub}}=\frac{V_d}{A}
=\frac{1800}{50}=36\text{ cm}
\]

Thus the freeboard is
\[
f=40-36=4.0\text{ cm}
\]

At the limiting condition, the top just reaches the water, so the entire cylinder is submerged:
\[
V_{d,\max}=AH=(50)(40)=2000\text{ cm}^3
\]
This corresponds to displaced water mass
\[
m_{\max}=\rho_w V_{d,\max}
=(1000)(2.00\times10^{-3})=2.00\text{ kg}
\]
The total mass already carried is \(1.80\text{ kg}\), so the largest further mass is
\[
\Delta m=2.00-1.80=0.20\text{ kg}=200\text{ g}
\]

Equivalently, the remaining \(4.0\text{ cm}\) of freeboard corresponds to volume
\[
A(4.0\text{ cm})=50(4)=200\text{ cm}^3
\]
and since \(200\text{ cm}^3\) of displaced water has mass \(200\text{ g}\), the check agrees.

\[
\boxed{\text{New freeboard }=4.0\text{ cm }(\approx 0.040\text{ m})}
\]
\[
\boxed{\text{Largest further mass it can carry }=0.20\text{ kg}=200\text{ g}}
\]

This assumes the added load itself does not displace water and the frictionless guide exerts no vertical force.
